translationRepairs: Before he was twenty-some years old he was already enfeoffed as a general, sharing rank with his father.
Before he was twenty-some years old he was already appointed as a general, sharing rank with his father.
拜將軍 is appointment to general's rank; 封 would be enfeoffment. The original 'enfeoffed' misreads 拜.
The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to read the heavens; Xianzhi was afraid to advance, and Bian Lingcheng was afraid as well.
The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to observe the sun; Lübing feared and did not wish to go on, and Bian Lingcheng also feared.
懼不欲行 has no 仙芝; the nearest agent is 韓履冰, and 邊令誠亦懼 pairs that fear with the envoy. The original invents Xianzhi as the fearful subject.
He ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge at once. Greater Bolü lay sixty li beyond; the bridge was severed only at dusk, and Tibetan forces were already pouring in — too late to stop them.
He ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge at once. Bolü still lay sixty li away; the bridge was severed only at dusk, and Tibetan forces were already pouring in — too late to stop them.
去勃律猶六十里 names 勃律, not 大勃律; 'Greater Bolü' is not in the Chinese.
In the ninth month they returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and rejoined Bian Lingcheng's detachment.
In the ninth month they returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and met Bian Lingcheng and the others.
與邊令誠等相見 is a meeting with Bian Lingcheng and others; 'detachment' is not in the Chinese.
When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one from the capital to welcome or comfort them; he cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one to welcome or comfort them; he cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
都不使人迎勞 says he sent no one to welcome them; it does not mention the capital.
Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from Shi he obtained more than ten large stones of kingfisher feathers, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in abundance.
Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from Shi he obtained more than ten large lumps of se-se gemstone, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in abundance.
大塊瑟瑟十餘石 are large lumps of se-se gemstone counted in 石, not kingfisher feathers.
if you judge by looks alone, you may lose another Zilu!"
if you judge by looks alone, you may lose another Ziyu!"
子羽 is Tantai Mieming's courtesy name in the Analects warning against judging by looks, not 子路 (Zilu).
if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose them as with Zilu!"
if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose them as with Ziyu!"
The literal likewise misreads 子羽 as Zilu; the source names Ziyu.

When his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty years of age, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was Commander-in-Chief — quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he had more than thirty personal attendants in memorial, their clothes bright and fresh.

When his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty years of age, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was Commander-in-Chief — quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he memorialized more than thirty personal attendants, their clothes bright and fresh.
奏傔從三十餘人 is listing or requesting attendants by memorial, not attendants who exist 'in memorial'.
Changqing sent his best horsemen against the Tujue vanguard and killed several hundred rebels.
Changqing sent his best horsemen against the Zhejie vanguard and killed several hundred rebels.
柘羯 are Central Asian Zhejie auxiliaries, not 突厥 (Tujue).
He withdrew to Xuaren Gate and was defeated again.
He withdrew to Xuanren Gate and was defeated again.
宣仁門 is Xuanren Gate; Xuaren drops the n of 仁.
I read in the Spring and Autumn that Langchen said he had not yet found his place to die — I have found mine.
I read in the Spring and Autumn that Lang Shen said he had not yet found his place to die — I have found mine.
狼瞫 is the Jin officer Lang Shen; Langchen fuses the surname 狼 and given name 瞫.
Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said, "Feng, you rose from nothing; I made you my judge, then you replaced me as commissioner, and today we die together — is this fate?"
Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said, "Feng the Second, you rose from nothing; I made you my judge, then you replaced me as commissioner, and today we die together — is this fate?"
封二 is the ranked address 'Feng the Second'; dropping 二 leaves only the surname.
He first served Commissioner Wang Yi; when Yi attacked Xincheng he put Han in charge of strategy, and the whole army stood in awe of him.
He first served Commissioner Wang Chui; when Chui attacked Xincheng he put Han in charge of strategy, and the whole army stood in awe of him.
王倕 is Wang Chui; Yi does not match 倕.
Han was summoned to court; the emperor was pleased with him and made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, prefect of Xiping, acting censor-in-chief, and Longyou commissioner in Zhongsi's place.

Han was summoned to court; the emperor was pleased with him and made him Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials (Honglu qing), prefect of Xiping, acting Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, and acting Longyou commissioner for disbursements and military colonies in Zhongsi's place, in charge of commission affairs.
鴻臚卿 is Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, not 開府/光祿 'Grand Master of Splendid Happiness'; 攝御史中丞 is Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, and 支度營田副大使，知節度事 must not be collapsed.
The emperor rewarded him with special advancement, acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, a fifth-rank post for a son, a thousand bolts of silk, a manor, and acting censor-in-chief.

The emperor rewarded him with Special Advancement, acting supernumerary Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, a fifth-rank post for a son, a thousand bolts of goods, a manor and a residence, and acting Censor-in-Chief.
鴻臚員外卿 is a supernumerary Honglu post, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; 物千匹 are bolts of goods, and 莊宅各一所 is a manor and a residence.

When An Lushan rebelled, after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi's defeats the emperor recalled Han and made him vanguard commander of the heir's army, with Tian Liangqiu as campaigning major and Wang Sili, Huoba Guiren, and others as deputies — two hundred thousand Hexi, Shuofang, and tribal troops with Xianzhi's veterans to hold Tong Pass.

When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
The original omits named deputies, 御史中丞, and 河隴 from 以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，以王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣及蕃將火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧等為裨將，河隴、朔方兵.
Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan held Hebei he lacked popular support — hold the pass, wear him down, let his followers split, and destroy him without heavy losses.
Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan had seized Hebei he lacked popular support — hold firm and wear them down, let them split of themselves, and destroy this bandit without heavy losses.
河朔 here is Hebei north of the Yellow River, not Shuofang; but 持重以弊之 is hold firm, not hold the pass, and 擒茲寇 is this bandit. The proposal's Hebei-Shuofang gloss is too specific.

Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian Henan, Lu Yong Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."

Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian is in Henan, Lu Jiong in Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
魯炅 is Lu Jiong, not Lu Yong, but the proposed line still fuses person and place as 'Lai Tian Henan' / 'Lu Jiong Nanyang'; 來填在河南，魯炅在南陽 needs the locatives.

Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Yong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."

Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Jiong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."
The literal already places each man with 在; only the romanization of 炅 as Yong is wrong and should be Jiong.
